records.title: AvalancheBench: Evaluating Enterprise Agent-Driven Semantic Query Processing Through Latent World Recovery
records.abstract: As LLMs improve, data agents are emerging as a new interface for analytics, while semantic query processing engines use LLMs to operate over structured and unstructured data. Existing benchmarks largely evaluate agents and semantic query engines in isolation, leaving it unclear whether agents can decide when and how to use semantic operators in end-to-end analysis. We introduce AvalancheBench, a multimodal enterprise analytics benchmark that generates observed data from latent world specifications and evaluates data agents on their ability to recover that world. The benchmark's 3 validated tasks contain 58 questions spanning text, images, and documents. Questions are provided together as a multi-part analytical brief and may share intermediate results, exposing the avalanche effect: errors can propagate through legitimate dependencies, and inappropriate reuse can cause otherwise unrelated questions to fail. AvalancheBench measures analytical fidelity, monetary cost, and capability-adjusted token cost (CATC), a new metric that weights token use by model capability to separate technical efficiency from provider pricing. We evaluate 5 model-harness configurations across 3 agent harnesses using Snowflake Cortex AISQL as the engine, with the best configuration reaching macro analytical fidelity of 0.82. Agents fail primarily in constructing the analysis: failing to recover facts that require semantic computation costs 45.1% of lost points, yet incorrect operator outputs account for only 2.5%, versus 36.3% from agents misusing or avoiding semantic operators. Misinterpreting requirements costs the most, at 51.5%. Errors also spread between questions: 29% of lost points come from reusing another question's results. Finally, monetary cost and CATC produce different Pareto frontiers, distinguishing economically attractive configurations from those that are technically resource efficient.

records.title: Creation of Customer Knowledge in a B2B Centred Innovation Ecosystem: A Single-Case Research
records.venue: European Conference on Knowledge Management
records.abstract: This study examines how B2B customer knowledge is created and managed within an innovation ecosystem, addressing a gap in prior research that has largely overlooked ecosystem-based perspectives on B2B customer knowledge creation. Drawing on knowledge management literature, particularly the knowledge-creating theory of the firm, and B2B marketing research, the study explores customer knowledge creation as an inter-organizational phenomenon. The research adopts a qualitative single-case study design focusing on a Finnish innovation ecosystem in its early development stage. Empirical data consist of semi-structured interviews supplemented with meetings, presentations, and field notes collected between 2025 and 2026. The focal company is a micro-enterprise developing a new B2B product concept. The findings indicate that B2B customer knowledge creation varies across different phases of new product development and occurs through two main processes. The first, externalization-based customer knowledge creation, involves transforming tacit knowledge held by B2B customers and end users into explicit knowledge through pilot projects, experimentation, and digital communication tools. The second, internalization-based customer knowledge creation, takes place primarily in the early stages of product development and relies on the firm’s own expertise, prior experience, and market-related knowledge rather than direct customer involvement. The study highlights the importance of distinguishing between B2B customers and end users, while emphasizing that both play crucial roles in knowledge creation within innovation ecosystems. It also suggests that effective customer knowledge creation can occur without long-term relationships, enabled instead by shared goals, cognitive proximity, and digital interaction.

records.title: Design and standardization of a new user-manager interface
records.venue: Economics. Finances. Law
records.abstract: The paper explores the transformation of priorities in the field of software development caused by changes in the relative value of technologies and human labor. These shifts urge developers to focus increasingly on the creation of efficient and user-friendly interfaces, particularly for managerial users within economic information systems. A variety of interface design approaches are considered, including user-centered design, goal-centered design, and activity-based interface modeling. The growing demand for both the creation of new user interfaces and the redesign of existing ones is emphasized as a significant trend in the modern IT market. The paper highlights four key criteria for evaluating interface quality: user performance speed, error rates, learning curve efficiency, and subjective satisfaction. These factors play a vital role in ensuring the success of enterprise information systems, which must support operational efficiency, seamless communication, and business process integration. Special attention is given to the importance of collaboration between end-users and developers throughout the design process. The research identifies that misalignment in perspectives - evident even during initial visual interactions with the interface – can lead to misunderstandings and functional mismatches. The paper also references relevant international standards (such as ISO 9241 and ISO/IEC 25010) and scientific contributions from Ukrainian and international scholars in the field of interface design. Overall, it underscores the strategic value of well-designed interfaces as communication channels between users and systems and presents design methodologies that can optimize user experience, reduce training costs, and improve the success rate of system implementation. Future research will focus on the development of standardized interface design principles, particularly using UX design practices and the implementation of adaptive interfaces that respond to the behavior and needs of enterprise managers.

records.title: Enhancing the User Interface of Open-Source Erp for Educational Use in Higher Education
records.venue: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Cryptography, Informatics, and Cybersecurity (ICoCICs)
records.abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems have become essential to modern organizations. As demand for ERP expertise grows, many universities have started incorporating ERP education into their curriculum. However, several challenges remain-such as the high cost of proprietary ERP and usability issues due to the complexity of the software-which make it difficult to teach ERP effectively. This paper aims to redesign the user interface of an open-source ERP system using the Design Thinking framework. iDempiere open-source ERP was chosen for this study as it has no licensing fees and has been implemented in companies all over the world-not only for business purposes but also for learning and teaching in some cases. A total of 12 students participated in usability testing and interview sessions, performing several tasks on the system's current interface. The results were analyzed through the five phases of Design Thinking: Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype and Test. The outcome was a high-fidelity prototype, which was then tested again using the usability testing and the System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaire. The results indicate improvements in the metrics collected during the testing, including an increase in the average SUS score from 46.46 to 89.17, as well as reduction in both task completion time and number of errors. These findings suggest that the redesigned UI successfully enhances the usability of the open-source ERP system.

records.title: From Coding Assistants to Self-Healing Terminals: NeuraOS A Critical Review of AI-Driven Autonomous Command Execution and Error Recovery on Linux Systems
records.venue: Iconic research and engineering journals
records.abstract: The Linux command-line interface continues to serve as the primary control surface for software development, systems administration, and cloud operations, yet it executes instructions syntactically, without semantic awareness of user intent and without built-in mechanisms for diagnosing or repairing runtime failures. Over roughly the last decade, three largely distinct research communities have each addressed part of this problem: large language model (LLM)-based coding assistants embedded in integrated development environments (IDEs), natural-language-to-command translation systems that lower the barrier to shell usage, and operating-systems research on self-healing and autonomic computing that targets distributed and cloud infrastructure rather than the interactive terminal. This paper presents a structured, critical review of these three strands, together with the log-based anomaly-detection and AIOps literature that supplies much of the diagnostic machinery such systems would require. Literature was retained where it addressed semantic command interpretation, real-time or near-real-time failure diagnosis, autonomous or semi-autonomous recovery, or persistence of prior failure-resolution experience. The reviewed work is organized along four analytical dimensions — runtime integration, autonomy level, diagnostic depth, and knowledge retention — and compared qualitatively across these dimensions. The synthesis shows that autonomy and diagnostic sophistication increase substantially when moving from IDE assistants toward self-healing infrastructure research, but this increase is accompanied by a shift away from the single-operator, single-machine terminal context, and that no reviewed system combines real-time in-terminal diagnosis, multi-pathway recovery, and durable per-machine experiential learning while remaining confined to user space. The review further discusses recurring safety and governance themes — confidence-gated autonomy, privilege-aware execution, and explanation-first human oversight — that constrain the design space for any terminal-level orchestration layer, and it identifies four concrete research gaps together with a near-, mid-, and long-term research roadmap. The review does not claim that any single technology described is either novel or previously unstudied in isolation; its contribution is the cross-domain synthesis and the identification of the specific combination of properties that remains unaddressed.

records.title: From static analytics to continuous intelligence: toward a dynamic model of real-time organizational decision systems
records.venue: Journal of Enterprise Information Management
records.abstract:
Enterprise decision systems increasingly couple time-sensitive sensing, workflow-embedded recommendations or actions, bounded machine discretion and operational feedback. This paper aims to develop a dynamic model of Continuous Intelligence (CI) that explains the organizational consequences of alignment or imbalance among these properties.
 
 
 
 The paper uses a problem-driven conceptual theory-building approach. It integrates and contrasts research on decision support, real-time and operational analytics, automation and delegation, hybrid intelligence, machine learning operations, AI capability and governance, information systems success and dynamic capabilities. The inferential pathway is documented through contrastive construct analysis, rejected alternative representations, mechanism mapping and conceptual boundary probing.
 
 
 
 CI is a four-dimensional decision-system configuration enabled by technical architecture, a CI governance process and human judgment integration. Its distinctive explanatory value lies in interaction effects: temporal continuity can amplify error propagation, discretion can amplify both value and harm, embedded feedback can create adaptive learning or self-reinforcing lock-in, and control design can compress or prolong intervention. Contextual alignment, rather than maximal automation, determines expected outcomes.
 
 
 
 The framework is conceptual and does not establish causal effects. It offers five multilevel propositions, falsification conditions and a sequenced research agenda for formative profile construction, configurational testing and longitudinal evaluation.
 
 
 
 The framework provides theory-informed governance heuristics for matching sensing cadence, decision authority, feedback and oversight to decision risk, reversibility and equivocality. It also identifies proportional implementation options and constraints for smaller organizations.
 
 
 
 The redistribution of decision authority from human agents toward AI systems is occurring without adequate governance frameworks in most enterprise deployments. At the industry level, correlated model behavior across organizations deploying similar CI architectures creates systemic risks including flash crashes in financial markets, cascade failures in logistics networks, and biased clinical triage at scale. The European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (EU AI Act) and equivalent regulatory frameworks are attempting to retrofit accountability structures onto CI deployments that outpaced governance development. This paper contributes the theoretical grounding needed to design accountability structures prospectively rather than reactively.
 
 
 
 The contribution is configurational and explanatory rather than technological. The paper shows how familiar decision-system properties generate emergent organizational effects when recursively coupled within operational workflows and why comparable investments can produce divergent outcomes.

records.title: From Trust Repair to Interaction Repairability: A Conceptual Framework for Recoverable Generative AI Experiences
records.venue: International journal of research and innovation in social science
records.abstract: Generative AI is now part of everyday writing, coding, design, education, and decision-support work, yet the interfaces around these systems are still weak when an output goes wrong. Research on reliability, trust repair, explainability, controllability, mental models, and conversational repair explains important parts of the problem, but gives less attention to a practical question: how should an interface help a user recover the work that has been affected? This conceptual paper introduces the Repairable Generative Interaction (RGI) Framework. It defines interaction repairability as the degree to which a human-AI system helps users detect a consequential breakdown, identify the affected objects and dependencies, understand the mismatch between intended and generated states, make a bounded correction, restore a coherent task state, and retain a traceable record of the recovery. The framework was developed through a problem-driven integrative synthesis of contemporary human-AI research and established HCI work on error recovery, undo, reversibility, and user control. RGI brings together six proposed failure classes, six recursive repair functions, four interaction layers, and five cross-cutting design commitments. It also distinguishes repairability from reliability, explainability, controllability, resilience, contestability, and trust repair, and proposes measurable indicators and seven testable propositions. A worked example from Malaysian open and distance learning shows how the framework can be applied without presenting it as empirical evidence. RGI remains a conceptual framework and now requires empirical testing across task recovery, user agency, mental-model accuracy, trust calibration, accessibility, cultural-linguistic variation, and governance contexts.

records.title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Computer Science and Software Engineering B2B Management and Lead Generation
Localization-Safe Error Recovery: Ensuring Comprehension and Operability Across Languages and Scripts in High-Integrity User Journeys
records.venue: International Journal of Engineering Science and Information Technology
records.abstract: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) has become a critical security mechanism for protecting digital services; however, the effectiveness of MFA depends heavily on the usability and reliability of account recovery processes. Existing evaluations of MFA recovery deployments report alarmingly high failure rates, with approximately one in two users unable to successfully complete recovery tasks under testing conditions even before localization factors are considered. This study investigates how localization influences recovery usability and argues that translation can systematically amplify recovery failures through predictable and classifiable mechanisms. Common issues include text expansion that truncates recovery instructions, grammatical reordering that displaces embedded identifiers, mixed bidirectional text that reverses verification codes, and typography-related height changes that obscure keyboard-focusable controls. These failures are not caused by linguistic inaccuracies but rather by correctly translated content interacting with interfaces that were not designed to accommodate the structural characteristics of target languages. To address this challenge, the study proposes a two-instrument engineering framework grounded in the principles of WCAG 2.2 accessibility standards. The first component is a recovery message schema that models required fields, interaction dependencies, and interface invariants across all recovery states. The second component is a localization hazard model that captures causal relationships among translation phenomena, structural interface failures, and resulting user harm. Together, these instruments establish a verifiable standard for localization-safe recovery design. A recovery workflow is considered localization-safe only when all schema properties are preserved, interaction invariants remain satisfied, and every identified hazard class within supported locales is mitigated through design and verification activities. The findings highlight that reliable recovery experiences cannot be achieved through linguistic review alone. Instead, localization safety must be embedded within release governance, verification architecture, accessibility testing, and localization management practices to ensure secure, inclusive, and globally deployable authentication systems?

records.title: Platform E-Business B2B Berbasis Blockchain untuk Meningkatkan Transparansi Rantai Pasok UMKM di Kabupaten Pesawaran
records.venue: Explore: Jurnal Sistem informasi dan telematika
records.abstract: -Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a crucial role in regional economies, yet they continue to face various challenges, particularly in supply chain transparency, market access, and transaction recording. This study aims to design a blockchain-based B2B e-business platform that can enhance trust and efficiency in business interactions among MSMEs in Pesawaran Regency. The system was developed using a Research and Development (R&D) approach with the ADDIE model, encompassing analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation phases. Hyperledger Fabric technology was employed to record every product data modification, creating a permanent and immutable audit trail. The findings demonstrate that the designed application successfully meets the primary functional requirements of MSMEs, including login functionality, sales and purchase transactions, inventory management, product data management, financial reporting, and product data version tracking. Compatibility testing shows that the system performs well across various devices and browsers, while functionality and Black Box Testing confirm that all features operate as designed. The blockchain implementation has proven effective in enhancing transparency, accountability, and trust among business stakeholders. This platform simultaneously serves as a digitalization tool that supports the competitiveness of local MSMEs in an increasingly competitive business ecosystem

records.title: Relationship between Customer Type and Communication Channels in Czech Enterprises
records.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Business Excellence
records.abstract: Abstract Customer orientation and communication with them are among the key factors in companies’ competitiveness in an environment of increasing digitization and changing customer behavior. Understanding how key customers are defined within companies and which communication channels are used to reach them is therefore essential amid changing market conditions. Current research shows that marketing communication in the B2B and B2C segments operates on different principles: B2B communication emphasizes building long-term relationships, value, and logical arguments to support purchasing decisions, while B2C communication focuses on emotional interaction, brand, and quick consumer decisions. The aim of this article is to evaluate the relationship between the structure of key customers and the communication channels used by Czech companies of various sizes and from different industries. Based on data from 153 companies operating in the Czech Republic, the relationship between customer orientation and the forms of marketing communication used was examined. Statistical methods included descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and PERMANOVA. The results showed that neither industry nor company size statistically explained differences in customer structure or in the choice of communication channels. The only significant factor was customer type. B2Boriented companies prefer personal, relationship-based forms of communication (direct sales, telephone contacts, professional events), while B2C companies systematically use digital communication mediums (web, social networks, email marketing). The article thus confirms that effective marketing communication is based primarily on understanding and segmenting customers, and on choosing channels that correspond to their decision-making behavior – areas at the core of the Business Model Canvas’s design and innovation.

records.title: SCALABLE MOBILE APPLICATION DESIGN SYSTEMS AND REUSABLE USER INTERFACE COMPONENTS FOR SAUDI ARABIA'S DIGITAL BANKING TRANSFORMATION
records.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research
records.abstract: Mobile banking in Saudi Arabia is increasingly the primary channel through which customers authenticate, transfer money, pay their bills and manage their financial relationships. The pace of feature delivery can, however, lead to a proliferation of interface inconsistencies, accessibility issues and duplicated effort. This review considers whether a scalable design system and a suite of reusable UI components can balance the need for efficient development with the particular requirements of the regulated financial services sector. A structured integrative synthesis is used to bring together the research on Saudi banking usability, digital adoption, accessibility, interface localisation, modular frontend engineering and cross-platform performance. The 30 publications identified via DOI (2020-2025) are interpreted through a clearly defined set of architectural and human-centred criteria rather than being aggregated into any form of unsupported effect estimate. The synthesis makes a clear distinction between visual reuse and behavioural/transactional reuse and proposes a layered design system model comprising governed tokens, accessible primitives, financial workflow patterns and institution-specific compositions. The findings suggest that standardisation is most likely to deliver benefit when the shared components encode accessible states, Arabic directionality, transaction disclosure, error recovery and security boundaries, with the potential for audited variation.

records.title: The design and development of an e-marketing framework for the Asian B2B market place
UML Functional Aspects in Business-to-Business: Some Lessons Learned
records.venue: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
records.abstract: In the early stages of software development, identifying, addressing, and resolving design issues is crucial to enhancing software quality and reducing costs. Techniques such as use case modeling and Unified Modeling Language (UML) scenario engineering have gained prominence in the elicitation of requirements, specification development, and the creation and interpretation of design documents. In recent years, Business-to-Business (B2B) collaboration has emerged as a key driver for the success of modern enterprises, especially within the rapidly evolving e-business landscape. Although various Business-to-Business protocols have been designed to facilitate these interactions, a universally accepted standard has yet to emerge. UML has played a significant role in the development of business information systems. This paper presents insights and best practices for applying UML scenario engineering in creating sequence diagrams, scenario extension, and developing Business-to-Business systems.
